section: Growth of nationalist poetry in Telugu - Gurajada, Rayaprolu, Garimella Satyanarayana
subsections: Patriotic plays and verse inspired by world events → author
Rayaprolu Subba Rao - works, genre, new poetic concept
Garimella Satyanarayana - song banned, imprisonment, collections

accepted.s: The lines “Desamunu preminchumanna, manchi annadi penchumanna” are associated with which poet and collection?
accepted.x: The lines were written by Gurajada Apparao and form part of Mutyala Saralu. The poem was published in Andhra Bharati.
accepted.tq: Use the poet–work pair directly; nearby nationalist poets are used as distractors.
accepted.sec: Nationalist songs → poet + collection

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly explains the idea expressed in the line “Desamante matti kadoi, desamante manushuloi”?
o: The nation is identified with its ruling dynasty.
The nation is represented only by its religious institutions.
The nation is defined by its geographical boundaries alone.
The nation consists primarily of its people rather than merely its soil.
accepted.x: Gurajada’s line means that a nation is its people, not merely its soil. It is part of the same poem in Mutyala Saralu.
accepted.tq: Translate the famous line into its precise underlying concept.
accepted.sec: Nationalist songs → poet + collection

accepted.s: The poem containing “Desamunu preminchumanna” was called the national anthem of the Telugu people. In which periodical was it published?
accepted.x: Gurajada Apparao’s poem was published in Andhra Bharati and came to be regarded as the national anthem of the Telugu people.
accepted.tq: Separate the collection, periodical and title-related details of the same poem.
accepted.sec: Nationalist songs → poet + collection

accepted.s: “Veera gandham tecchinaramu” is associated with which movement or period?
accepted.x: “Veera gandham tecchinaramu” was written by Tripuraneni Ramaswamy during the Salt Satyagraha era.
accepted.tq: Match the song with its historical occasion rather than merely its poet.
accepted.sec: Nationalist songs → poet + collection

accepted.s: Who wrote the patriotic lyric “Ye desamegina ... pogadara nee talli bhoomi Bharatini”, commonly known by its title Janmabhoomi?
accepted.x: The patriotic lyric Janmabhoomi was written by Rayaprolu Subbarao.
accepted.tq: Identify the author from a distinctive line and title.
accepted.sec: Nationalist songs → poet + collection

accepted.s: “Bharata khandambu chakkani paadi aavu” was improvised on which occasion?
o: During the Salt Satyagraha at Dandi in 1930
During Bipin Chandra Pal’s speeches at Rajahmundry in April 1907
During the Home Rule agitation in Madras in 1916
During Gandhi’s visit to Vijayawada in 1921
accepted.x: Chilakamarti Lakshmi Narasimham improvised the song during Bipin Chandra Pal’s speeches at Rajahmundry in April 1907.
accepted.tq: Lock the answer through the distinctive place, speaker and month-year combination.
accepted.sec: Nationalist songs → poet + collection

accepted.s: “Ma Telugu Talliki mallepoodanda” later acquired which status?
o: It became the anthem of the Andhra University.
It became the official anthem of the Indian National Congress.
It became the national song of India.
It became the Andhra Pradesh State song.
accepted.x: The song written by Sankarambadi Sundarachari later became the Andhra Pradesh State song.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a state song from national and organisational anthems.
accepted.sec: Nationalist songs → poet + collection

accepted.s: Who was known by the title “Abhinava Nannaya” according to the commission’s key and the accepted examination reference?
accepted.x: The accepted examination answer is Rayaprolu Subbarao. Although another source assigns the title to Viswanatha, the commission’s key and CDI assign it to Rayaprolu.
accepted.tq: Resolve a source-sensitive title by remembering the examination-key convention rather than the conflicting attribution.
accepted.sec: Poets' popular titles → poet

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Devulapalli Krishna Sastri was known as Andhra Shelley. Kavi Kokila is associated with Duvvuri Ramireddy, Telugu Lenka with Tummala Sitaramamurthy, and Kavi Samrat with Viswanatha Satyanarayana.
accepted.tq: Use elimination among closely related poet titles and avoid confusing popular epithets.
accepted.sec: Poets' popular titles → poet

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the titles associated with Gurram Jashuva is correct?
o: He was given Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti in 1946.
He was known as Andhra Shelley.
He received Viswakavi Samrat in 1936 from Vinukonda citizens.
He received Madhura Kavi Srinatha in 1964.
accepted.x: Gurram Jashuva was given the title Navayuga Kavi Chakravarti in 1946. He also had the titles Madhura Kavi Srinatha in 1952 and Viswakavi Samrat in 1964; Vinukonda citizens gave him Kavi Kokila in 1936.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among a poet’s multiple titles by checking the title-year association.
accepted.sec: Poets' popular titles → poet

accepted.s: The title “Kavi Kokila” is associated with which poet, while it was also given to Gurram Jashuva by Vinukonda citizens in 1936?
accepted.x: Kavi Kokila is associated with Duvvuri Ramireddy. Vinukonda citizens also conferred the same title on Gurram Jashuva in 1936.
accepted.tq: Notice that one title can have both a conventional association and a separate conferral.
accepted.sec: Poets' popular titles → poet

accepted.s: Who conferred the title “Madhurakavi” on Gurram Jashuva?
accepted.x: The title Madhurakavi was given to Gurram Jashuva by Viswanatha Satyanarayana.
accepted.tq: Identify the person who conferred a title, not merely the person who held it.
accepted.sec: Poets' popular titles → poet

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Poet)
a. Rayaprolu Subbarao
b. Gurajada Apparao
c. Viswanatha Satyanarayana
d. Unnava Lakshminarayana

List-II (Work)
i. Malapalli
ii. Andhravali
iii. Kanyasulkam
iv. Veyipadagalu

Select the correct code:
accepted.x: Rayaprolu wrote Andhravali, Gurajada wrote Kanyasulkam, Viswanatha wrote Veyipadagalu, and Unnava wrote Malapalli.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and verify that every remaining work is used exactly once.
accepted.sec: Poets → works (match format)

accepted.s: Which of the following works was written by Duvvuri Ramireddy?
accepted.x: Matru Desa Sankeertanam was written by Duvvuri Ramireddy. Swatantrya Rathamu is by Rayaprolu, Desabhakti Geyam by Gurajada, and Firdausi by Gurram Jashuva.
accepted.tq: Use direct author–work recall with works from neighbouring poets as distractors.
accepted.sec: Poets → works (match format)

accepted.s: Kanyasulkam, first staged in 1893, was written by whom?
accepted.x: Kanyasulkam was written by Gurajada Apparao and was staged in 1893.
accepted.tq: Combine a work’s author with its distinctive staging year.
accepted.sec: Poets → works (match format)

accepted.s:
Which one of the following statements is correct regarding Viswanatha Satyanarayana’s works?
1. Veyipadagalu received the Sahitya Akademi recognition.
2. Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu won the Jnanpith.
3. Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu was the first Jnanpith-winning work by a Telugu writer.
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Veyipadagalu received Sahitya Akademi recognition, while Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu won the Jnanpith and was the first such award for a Telugu writer.
accepted.tq: Check the separate award associations before choosing the inclusive statement option.
accepted.sec: Poets → works (match format)

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Gabbilam was written by Gurram Jashuva, not Duvvuri Ramireddy. Duvvuri Ramireddy wrote Matru Desa Sankeertanam.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped author–work pair among otherwise familiar literary associations.
accepted.sec: Poets → works (match format)

accepted.s: Who wrote Japaneeyamu, which celebrated Japan’s victory over Russia in 1905?
accepted.x: Japaneeyamu was written by Sriram Veerabrahmam of Bandar and celebrated Japan’s victory over Russia in 1905.
accepted.tq: Match the world event and patriotic work with the correct author.
accepted.sec: Patriotic plays and verse inspired by world events → author

accepted.s: Adipudi Somanatha Rao’s Japan Charitra was dedicated to whom?
accepted.x: Japan Charitra by Adipudi Somanatha Rao was dedicated to the Raja of Munagala. The Raja named his sons Togo and Nogi after Japanese commanders.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the dedicatee of a work from the historical figures who inspired it.
accepted.sec: Patriotic plays and verse inspired by world events → author

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Panchala Parabhavam:
1. It was written by Damaraju Pundarikakshudu.
2. It dealt with the Jallianwala Bagh tragedy.
3. Dyer was portrayed as Duryodhana.
4. Twenty-five students in Vizag were arrested for staging it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The play concerned Jallianwala Bagh, cast Dyer as Duryodhana, was discussed in the British Parliament, and led to the arrest of 25 Vizag students who staged it.
accepted.tq: Treat the play, event, characterisation and consequence as separate factual components.
accepted.sec: Patriotic plays and verse inspired by world events → author

accepted.s: Which pair is correctly matched with the year of the patriotic play?
accepted.x: Padmavyuham was written by Kallakuri Narayana Rao in 1919. Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam was written by Umar Alisha in 1916.
accepted.tq: Check the author–title–year triad and reject swapped playwrights.
accepted.sec: Patriotic plays and verse inspired by world events → author

accepted.s:
Arrange the following works in chronological order of the years given:
A. Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam
B. Japan’s victory over Russia celebrated in Japaneeyamu
C. Padmavyuham
D. Kanyasulkam was staged
accepted.x: Kanyasulkam was staged in 1893, Japan’s victory occurred in 1905, Mahabharata Kaurava Rangam was written in 1916, and Padmavyuham in 1919.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the two middle events.
accepted.sec: Patriotic plays and verse inspired by world events → author

accepted.s: Rayaprolu Subba Rao is best known as the Father of which literary movement in Telugu?
accepted.x: Rayaprolu Subba Rao is called the Father of Telugu Romanticism.
accepted.tq: Identify the literary movement associated with a distinctive honorific.
accepted.sec: Rayaprolu Subba Rao - works, genre, new poetic concept

accepted.s: Which literary form did Rayaprolu Subba Rao pioneer in Telugu, drawing inspiration from Shelley and Keats?
accepted.x: Rayaprolu pioneered Bhava Kavitvam, or poetry centred on emotion, drawing on Shelley and Keats.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact literary term from similarly formed alternatives.
accepted.sec: Rayaprolu Subba Rao - works, genre, new poetic concept

accepted.s: What was the new poetic concept introduced by Rayaprolu Subba Rao?
accepted.x: Rayaprolu introduced Amalina Srungaram, a concept of platonic love.
accepted.tq: Pair the exact technical term with its stated meaning.
accepted.sec: Rayaprolu Subba Rao - works, genre, new poetic concept

accepted.s: Which of the following best describes Rayaprolu Subba Rao’s contribution to Telugu poetry?
o: He restored rigid prosody as the sole basis of Telugu poetry.
He replaced original verse with exclusively devotional compositions.
He moved away from translation of Sanskrit epics and introduced original, emotive verse.
He continued translating Sanskrit epics without alteration.
accepted.x: Rayaprolu broke with the translation of Sanskrit epics and brought original, emotive verse into Telugu. He also helped free Telugu poetry from rigid prosody.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that captures the complete literary change rather than an isolated label.
accepted.sec: Rayaprolu Subba Rao - works, genre, new poetic concept

accepted.s: Who described Rayaprolu’s romanticism as “escapist”?
o: Progressive writers such as Sri Sri
accepted.x: Progressive writers such as Sri Sri criticised Rayaprolu’s romanticism as escapist, even though he had an important role in freeing Telugu verse from rigid prosody.
accepted.tq: Separate later critical assessment from the poet’s own literary contribution.
accepted.sec: Rayaprolu Subba Rao - works, genre, new poetic concept

accepted.s: Rayaprolu Subba Rao was born in which year and place?
accepted.x: Rayaprolu Subba Rao was born in 1892 at Guntur.
accepted.tq: Use the paired birth year and birthplace to distinguish Rayaprolu from other poets.
accepted.sec: Rayaprolu Subba Rao - works, genre, new poetic concept

accepted.s: Garimella Satyanarayana left his studies in response to whose call?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal’s call for Swadeshi
Sri Sri’s call for progressive literature
Rayaprolu Subba Rao’s call for romantic poetry
accepted.x: Garimella Satyanarayana left his studies in response to Mahatma Gandhi’s call during the freedom movement.
accepted.tq: Identify the leader associated with the decisive personal action.
accepted.sec: Garimella Satyanarayana - song banned, imprisonment, collections

accepted.s: Garimella Satyanarayana lived during which period?
accepted.x: Garimella Satyanarayana lived from 14 July 1893 to 18 December 1952.
accepted.tq: Read the complete date range carefully; similar day-month reversals are the trap.
accepted.sec: Garimella Satyanarayana - song banned, imprisonment, collections

accepted.s: Garimella Satyanarayana was born at which place?
accepted.x: Garimella Satyanarayana was born at Gonedapadu in Narasannapeta taluk of Srikakulam.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the poet’s village, taluk and district from the birthplaces of other literary figures.
accepted.sec: Garimella Satyanarayana - song banned, imprisonment, collections

accepted.s: For how long was Garimella Satyanarayana jailed in 1922 for his nationalist song?
accepted.x: He was jailed in 1922 for one year for the song “Maakoddee Tella Doratanamu.” A later sentence involved two and a half years of rigorous imprisonment.
accepted.tq: Separate the first sentence from the later rigorous-imprisonment term.
accepted.sec: Garimella Satyanarayana - song banned, imprisonment, collections

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT listed as a grievance in Garimella Satyanarayana’s nationalist song?
accepted.x: The song listed grievances such as taxes, forced labour, untouchability and the policy of divide and rule. Expansion of scientific education was not among the listed grievances.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated item among the specific grievances named in the song.
accepted.sec: Garimella Satyanarayana - song banned, imprisonment, collections

accepted.s: Which statement about the circulation and reception of Garimella Satyanarayana’s nationalist song is correct?
o: It was cyclostyled a thousand times and praised by Gandhi.
It was published exclusively in a British government journal.
It was printed only once and was ignored by Gandhi.
It was circulated only among literary associations after independence.
accepted.x: The song was cyclostyled a thousand times and was praised by Mahatma Gandhi.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive circulation figure and prominent response as a paired fact.
accepted.sec: Garimella Satyanarayana - song banned, imprisonment, collections

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a work or category associated with Garimella Satyanarayana?
accepted.x: Ramayana Kalpavrikshamu was written by Viswanatha Satyanarayana. Garimella’s works included Harijana Paatalu, anti-liquor songs, Samajika Navala and Palletullalo.
accepted.tq: Use the author–work association to reject a famous work belonging to another poet.
accepted.sec: Garimella Satyanarayana - song banned, imprisonment, collections

accepted.s: Garimella Satyanarayana is described as which of the following?
o: The first people’s poet of the freedom struggle
accepted.x: Garimella Satyanarayana is called the first people’s poet of the freedom struggle.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a popular descriptive title from titles belonging to other Telugu literary figures.
accepted.sec: Garimella Satyanarayana - song banned, imprisonment, collections

accepted.s: Garimella Satyanarayana inspired which of the following group of writers and performers?
o: Sri Sri, Viswanatha and Unnava Lakshminarayana
accepted.x: Garimella inspired Nazar, Subbarao Panigrahi and Gaddar.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete influence-group rather than selecting a single familiar name.
accepted.sec: Garimella Satyanarayana - song banned, imprisonment, collections

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Garimella Satyanarayana:
1. His nationalist song was associated with the Non-Cooperation era.
2. He received a later sentence of two and a half years of rigorous imprisonment.
3. His wife, father and grandfather died while he was in jail.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The song belonged to the Non-Cooperation era, he later received two and a half years of rigorous imprisonment, and three close family members died during his imprisonment.
accepted.tq: Combine movement context, punishment and personal consequence without confusing the two imprisonment terms.
accepted.sec: Garimella Satyanarayana - song banned, imprisonment, collections
